newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cuts beef export licence validity.
newsitem.headline: EU cuts beef export licence validity.

text.p: The European Union on Friday cut the period of validity of beef export licences to 30 days from the current month plus one month in a move to stop speculative applications, a Commission official said.

The move follows last week's 10 percent cut in export refunds which followed a rush of licence applications. The cut led to protests, led by Irish farm minister Ivan Yates at the EU farm Council on Monday.
Yates told the Council that other methods could be used to discourage exports which are subject to a GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) annual limit.
But Friday's decision taken at the EU sheep management committee does not include restitution of the export refund cut.
The Commission pointed out that the EU is 65 percent of the way towards its GATT limit of 1.187 million tonnes a year a little over six months into the 1996/1997 July-June period.
An EU official told Reuters that the Commission is concerned about what it sees as recent speculative applications.

A Commission official said that cutting the period of validity for licences will mean that traders will have to be certain of their contracts before applying for licences. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800 Chris White
